sources.title: Claude 3 Haiku: our fastest model yet
sources.evidence: Dated March 13, 2024; announces immediate availability of Claude 3 Haiku in the Claude API and Claude Pro, with vision capabilities.

sources.title: Introducing the next generation of Claude
sources.evidence: The March 4, 2024 family announcement names Claude 3 Haiku but says its availability is forthcoming. Specifies an initial production context of 200K tokens for all three Claude 3 models.

sources.title: The Claude 3 Model Family: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, including June and October 2024 addenda
sources.evidence: Fetched directly and extracted with pdftotext after the web reader could not fetch the redirect. Names Anthropic as developer, specifies text/image input with text output and 200K production context. Original and later addendum comparisons include Claude 3 Haiku but report no numeric total or active parameter count. Relative parameter scaling is discussed without counts.

sources.title: Model deprecations
sources.evidence: Maps Claude Haiku 3 to claude-3-haiku-20240307; documents February 19, 2026 deprecation and April 20, 2026 retirement. Retired models are unavailable on Anthropic-operated platforms; partner platforms have their own schedules.

sources.title: Unsupervised Elicitation of Language Models — original Anthropic-hosted paper
sources.evidence: Section 3.3 explicitly contrasts open-weight Llama models with proprietary Claude 3 Haiku and Claude 3.5 Haiku. The experimental default is pretrained models before post-training; section 4.4 distinguishes the Haiku 3 reward model from the Haiku 3.5 assistant. No numeric Haiku parameter counts are supplied. This wording was verified in the original 13-page hosted paper, not assumed from the newer 18-page arXiv revision.

sources.title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
sources.evidence: Methods Notes explicitly includes production Haiku 3 among the studied Claude models and describes recording and injecting activations into layer residual streams. The introduction and discussion describe the studied model architectures as Transformer-based. This supports only the coarse Transformer classification, not dense/MoE routing or numeric size.

sources.title: Claude can now use tools
sources.evidence: May 30, 2024 announcement makes tool use generally available across the entire Claude 3 family, explicitly discussing Haiku tool-use deployments.

sources.title: Claude 3 Haiku — Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Exact Bedrock model ID anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0; lists March 13, 2024 model launch, 200K context, image/text inputs and text output. The service has region-dependent legacy status; documentation is not an endpoint test.

sources.title: Partner model deprecations — Claude 3 Haiku on Google Cloud
sources.evidence: Retained exact Haiku 3 section lists text/code/images in and text out, 200K context, function calling, and extended thinking as unsupported. Its Documents row points to Anthropic PDF support. March 19, 2024 is this provider's launch date, not earliest public availability. The page retains future-tense shutdown language after the stated August 23, 2026 date, so it is historical capability documentation rather than current availability proof.

sources.title: Citations API and PDF support for Claude models now in Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: June 30, 2025 launch lists PDF support for Opus 4, Sonnet 4, Sonnet 3.7 and Sonnet 3.5v2; Haiku 3 is not among its supported models. This establishes that launch's scope, not a permanent prohibition on later provider processing of PDFs.

sources.title: Models.dev Claude Haiku 3 record
sources.evidence: Followed the baseline source. It lists PDF input and the compatibility description; used only to identify assertions requiring independent verification.

name.note: Anthropic's current lifecycle naming is Claude Haiku 3; launch-era naming was Claude 3 Haiku. Both identify this exact API model.

developer.note: Confirmed by the developer announcement and model card.

family.note: Retains the catalog's Haiku-line family key; the model belongs to the Claude 3 generation.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public availability is March 13. March 4 was the family announcement with Haiku forthcoming; 20240307 is the snapshot identifier, and March 19 was Google Cloud's later launch.

open_weights.note: Anthropic's paper explicitly classifies Claude 3 Haiku as proprietary in contrast to open-weight models. Its experimental default concerns the pretrained model; the public API snapshot is the post-trained product. This is not inferred solely from API hosting.

license.note: Proprietary is the explicit developer classification, not a named open-weight redistribution license.

parameters_b.note: No numeric total is disclosed in the original card, later Claude 3.5 addendum comparisons naming Haiku 3, or the reviewed exact-model training and interpretability papers. Unofficial estimates are not accepted.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-parameter count or dense/MoE routing disclosure was found in the reviewed primary sources; it cannot be equated to an unknown total.

architecture.note: Coarse classification supported by the first-party paper's explicit production Haiku 3 scope, residual-stream layer interventions and Transformer-based architecture discussion. Dense versus MoE, layer count, and other internal dimensions remain undisclosed.

context_window.note: Public production context is 200K tokens; the research demonstration beyond 1M tokens does not establish a public 1M window.

modalities.note: Text/image input and text output are explicit. PDF is retained narrowly as a provider-documented input format: Google's exact Haiku 3 Documents row links PDF support. It is not a separate neural modality or proof of native Anthropic Messages PDF blocks. AWS's June 2025 PDF launch excludes Haiku 3 from its listed scope, so PDF handling is provider-dependent and less directly documented than text/image.

reasoning.note: The exact Haiku 3 capability table explicitly marks extended thinking unsupported. False denotes absence of that dedicated reasoning mode, not inability to solve reasoning tasks or follow chain-of-thought prompts.

tool_call.note: Tool/function calling is explicitly documented for the Claude 3 family and Haiku 3; general availability followed the model launch on May 30, 2024.

description.value: Anthropic's compact Claude 3 model for fast text and image tasks, with a 200K-token context window and tool use. Retired from the Claude API on April 20, 2026.
description.note: Replaces the unsupported present-tense claim that the model remains available for compatibility. Retirement is scoped to the Claude API because partner schedules differ.

patch.description: Anthropic's compact Claude 3 model for fast text and image tasks, with a 200K-token context window and tool use. Retired from the Claude API on April 20, 2026.
patch.notes: Publicly released March 13, 2024 after the March 4 family announcement; 20240307 is the snapshot identifier. Total and active parameter counts and dense/MoE routing remain undisclosed. Transformer classification is supported by Anthropic's exact-model interpretability research. PDF is retained as a provider-documented input format from Google's Haiku 3 Documents row; native PDF-block support on the Anthropic API is not established, and AWS's June 2025 PDF launch listed newer models only. Claude API retirement was April 20, 2026; historical capability documentation does not establish current partner endpoint availability.

sources.label: Claude 3 model card and later comparisons

summary: All 14 fields reviewed. Confirms March 13, 2024 public release, 200K context, text/image-to-text capability, tool use and no extended-thinking mode. Adds explicit proprietary classification and coarse Transformer architecture; leaves total/active counts undisclosed after later comparison and exact-model research checks. Corrects the compatibility description to the documented Claude API retirement. PDF is retained only under the catalog's provider-input-format interpretation, with Google/AWS documentation differences and lack of verified native Anthropic PDF-block support clearly recorded for parent review.
